# An actual balanced cap mixture is not ordered with uniform simplex measure

The mass and barycenter conservation in `candidate b6ffecfff4f39a35` does not imply convex-order domination in either direction, even for one actual family of proper common-centroid tetrahedral sections. The example below also comes from strictly positive stationary capacity rows. It is not claimed to be a capacity global maximum.

Let mu be uniform probability on Delta_3 and take the actual raw normals

    c_1=(7,12,-28,-28),
    c_2=(12,7,-28,-28),
    c_3=(-19,-19,56,56).

Their sum is zero. Every cut is a strict quadrilateral and its actual barycentric section centroid is

    b=(56,56,19,19)/150.                            (1)

For the first two cuts this follows by the quadrilateral diagonal points (12,7,3,3)/25 and (7,12,3,3)/25. Their raw plane values are positive multiples of the displayed c_1,c_2. The section-centroid formula (sum of the four section vertices minus the diagonal intersection)/3 gives (1). For the third plane its equation is xi_0+xi_1=56/75. It is a product of two segments with uniform section measure, whose two conditional pairs of means give (1) directly. These computations also appear as a geometric calibration in `candidate 5c1f3bb21840ea60`.

Let H_i={c_i dot xi>=0}, P_i=mu(H_i), and f_i the density at zero of sum_j c_ij Exp_j. Actual integration gives

    P=(4/25,4/25,354368/421875),
    f=(1/100,1/100,2128/421875),
    T=sum P_i/f_i=3772/19.                          (2)

For example a two-positive/two-negative raw vector (p,q,-r,-s) has

    f=[pq(r+s)+rs(p+q)]/[(p+r)(p+s)(q+r)(q+s)].

Its cap fraction is the formula (3) in the cap-variance source. Substituting gives every number in (2); reversal of a cut leaves f unchanged.

Define the actual conserved probability density

    w=(1/T) sum_i 1_Hi/f_i.

By the proved first-moment identity it has exactly the uniform simplex centroid. Nevertheless the probability measure w mu and mu are incomparable in convex order.

## 1. A convex quadratic decreases

For f_-(xi)=(xi_0-xi_1)^2, the exact cap integrals are

    int_H1 f_- dmu=int_H2 f_- dmu=37/1000,
    int_H3 f_- dmu=742504448/11865234375.

They yield

    int f_- w dmu=10583879/106087500,
    int f_- dmu=1/10,

and therefore

    int f_- (w-1) dmu=-24871/106087500<0.            (3)

Here is an exact reproducible integration rule for those cap moments. For a raw two-positive cap with captured vertices i,j and excluded vertices k,l, let A,B,C,D be its edge intersections on ik,il,jl,jk. The cap is triangulated by

    (e_i,A,B,C), (e_i,A,C,D), (e_i,e_j,C,D).

Each sub-tetrahedron's relative volume is the absolute determinant of its four barycentric vertices. For four barycentric vertices v_1,...,v_4, its conditional second-moment matrix is

    [sum_a v_a v_a^T+(sum_a v_a)(sum_a v_a)^T]/20.

This follows immediately from E Lambda_a Lambda_b=(1+1_(a=b))/20 for uniform tetrahedral barycentric coordinates. Multiplication by the three determinant volumes and summation gives the displayed exact integrals. Thus (3) is an actual polynomial integral, not an empirical covariance calculation.

## 2. A convex hinge increases

Put y=xi_0+xi_1 and f_+(xi)=(y-4/5)_+. On its positive support y>4/5, both c_1 dot xi and c_2 dot xi are positive: each is at least 7y-28(1-y)=35y-28>0. Also c_3 dot xi=56-75y<0. Consequently w is CONSTANT on this entire hinge support:

    w=200/T=950/943.

Under uniform tetrahedral measure y has density 6y(1-y) on [0,1]. Thus

    int f_+ dmu=int_(4/5)^1 (y-4/5)6y(1-y)dy=9/1250,

and

    int f_+(w-1)dmu=(7/943)(9/1250)=63/1178750>0.   (4)

Equations (3)--(4) use two continuous convex functions on the same compact simplex. They rule out both w mu <=_cx mu and mu <=_cx w mu.

## 3. Positive stationary rows really are available

The unnormalized proper thresholds t_i=P_i/f_i are

    (16,16,3164/19).

Set x_i=(t_i 1-c_i)/T. Explicitly,

    x_1=(9,4,44,44)/T,
    x_2=(4,9,44,44)/T,
    x_3=(3525,3525,2100,2100)/(19T).

All entries are strictly positive, and each column sums to one. Their actual threshold cuts t_i/T have precisely the displayed raw normals, up to the common positive scale 1/T. By coarea, threshold stationarity is t_i L_i=3P_i. It is a genuine global minimizing threshold for its positive row: the captured-volume cube root is concave in the threshold on the interval from the smallest row entry onward, and its tangent at the displayed point passes through the origin. Concavity therefore places the entire root-volume graph below that tangent, giving the defining capacity ratio minimum. Below the smallest entry there is no positive captured mass.

With objective weights P_i^(1/3), the differentiable capacity gradients at these rows equal the same b in (1), so this is an actual stationary column-stochastic configuration. No assertion of global maximality is made: the independently proved joint-curvature mechanisms can exclude such a stratum at a least-active global maximum.

The obstruction is therefore precisely scoped. Actual proper sections, common section centroid, full raw-normal balance, positive stationary rows, and exact mass/barycenter conservation do not suffice for a fixed convex-order transport to or from uniform simplex measure. A valid transport route must use additional optimizing, incidence, or curvature information.
